theme: Production readiness of a Node.js 22 / strict TypeScript npm-workspaces monorepo (parcel-tracking API + polling worker on Kubernetes, knex/PostgreSQL migrations, two published merchant packages, cucumber specifications): almost ready, with realistic gaps in test reliability, schema migrations, package publishing, executable specifications, Kubernetes runtime hardening and the classic readiness rows

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: apps/tracking-service/tests/unit/share-links.test.ts
entries.rationale: The test compares the link's expiry with an expected value it computes from a second, independent read of the wall clock (whole seconds since the epoch plus the fifteen-minute lifetime). When the clock crosses a second boundary between the read inside the code under test and the read in the assertion, the two differ by one and the test fails; otherwise it passes. The failure is rare (the window is the few microseconds between the two reads) but real and unrelated to any code change: a non-deterministic test.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: apps/tracking-service/tests/integration/poller.test.ts
entries.rationale: The test starts the carrier poller on real timers with a short interval, sleeps a fixed wall-clock time and then asserts a minimum number of completed polls. Each poll re-arms its timer only after its database and carrier work completes, so the count within the sleep depends on how loaded the machine is: on an idle machine it passes, on a busy CI runner (or with other test files running in parallel workers) it can fall short and fail. Ordering a test against background work with a fixed sleep instead of a signal is a non-deterministic test.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: At worker start-up the delivery log table is created from code when it does not exist (a schema-builder create-table behind an existence check), outside the versioned knex migrations that own every other table. The production schema now has a table no migration created, the migration history does not describe the database, a later migration that alters it fails on a fresh environment, and a column added to this code is never applied to an existing database. The worker's auto-create is the knex form of creating the schema from the model at runtime.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: @parcel-tracking/client
entries.rationale: The published client's latest release is a MINOR version whose changelog entry itself lists a removed public method and a renamed field of a returned type. Both break consumers that upgrade within their declared caret range. Under the semantic versioning the package declares, a breaking change requires a new major version.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: @parcel-tracking/webhooks
entries.rationale: The published webhook-verification package declares only `main` and `types`: no `exports` map and no `files` allow-list. Every file of the package directory is published (sources, tests, tsconfig) and every module under the build output - including the internal signature helpers - is importable by deep path, so each internal refactor is a potential breaking change for consumers. The public surface is not controlled. (Whole manifest: the defect is what it does not declare.)

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A Gherkin feature specifying the return-to-sender behaviour sits outside the paths of every cucumber profile (the default profile loads the tracking features, the webhooks profile the webhook features), so it is never executed by any test run or CI job; several of its steps have no step definition. It reads as an executable specification and is documentation that cannot fail.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: `code.startsWith("DL") || code.startsWith("DLV")`: every code starting with DLV also starts with DL, so the second operand can never decide the result and the condition is wider than it reads. It maps the carrier's delivery-exception code family (DLX...) to delivered, which is the behavioural defect the dead operand hides.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The egress allowance for the migration Job is `ipBlock 0.0.0.0/0` with no port restriction and no exceptions (the managed database's address is not stable). The pod that holds the schema-owner database credentials can therefore reach any address on any port - the cloud metadata endpoint, cluster-internal services, the internet - although it needs exactly one: the database port in the database subnet.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The migration Job's pod security context sets runAsNonRoot and the user, but no seccomp profile (neither RuntimeDefault nor Localhost), unlike both Deployments; its container sets none either, so the Job runs Unconfined on nodes whose runtime default is not enforced.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The namespace carries Pod Security Admission labels for `warn` and `audit` at the restricted level but no `enforce` label, so admission enforces nothing: a pod violating the restricted profile (the migration Job above, or a privileged container) is admitted with a warning. The team's intended admission gate is not on.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Merchant webhooks are POSTed with a bare fetch: no AbortSignal or timeout (undici's defaults allow minutes for headers and body), and a failure is only recorded for the next poll cycle. A merchant endpoint that accepts the connection and stalls blocks the sequential dispatch loop. The carrier client in the same worker sets the bar the team itself uses (a per-attempt timeout and bounded retries).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: `pollOnce` receives the worker's AbortSignal and checks it between parcels, but does not pass it to the carrier request, so a shutdown waits for every in-flight carrier call (up to its timeout and retries) instead of aborting it: the signal the method accepts is dropped at the one I/O call it makes.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The merchant delivery-statistics route is registered on a router that the app mounts before the authentication middleware (src/http/app.ts) and it checks neither a scope nor that the caller is the merchant in the path: any anonymous client can read any merchant's delivery figures by id. Every other `/v1` route requires a token and a named scope.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The redirect endpoint force-asserts the untyped request body to its request type and passes it on unvalidated: an oversized pickup point id, an unknown field, a hold date in the past or a missing field reach the service and the database while the type checker vouches for them. Every other body and parameter in the API is parsed with its zod schema. (The TypeScript form of missing inbound validation; the precise concept is named.)

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Webhook delivery outcomes and failures are written with console.log/console.error instead of the injected structured logger: no level, no merchant or delivery fields, no correlation with the poll that produced them, while the rest of the worker logs through pino.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The carrier readiness check catches every exception in an empty catch block and reports the carrier as reachable, so a carrier outage never shows on the readiness endpoint.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A warning is logged with a template literal that interpolates the carrier code and HTTP status into the message, instead of a pino object argument with a constant message: the values are not queryable fields and every message is a distinct string.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: apps/tracking-service/tests/unit/share-link-verification.test.ts
entries.rationale: Link expiry is tested with vitest fake timers and a fixed system time: the clock only moves when the test advances it, so the boundary checks (valid at the last second, rejected one second later) are deterministic.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: apps/tracking-service/tests/unit/retry.test.ts
entries.rationale: The retry and backoff tests involve real-looking delays, but every delay runs on fake timers advanced explicitly by the test (virtual time); nothing depends on the wall clock or machine load.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: apps/tracking-service/tests/integration/webhook-dispatch.test.ts
entries.rationale: The dispatch tests run the worker's dispatch loop on real timers but wait for the observable outcome with a condition polled to a generous timeout, not a fixed sleep; they pass as soon as the work is done and do not depend on how fast the machine is.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A versioned migration that creates the carriers table only when it does not exist: the table predates the service in the legacy database it adopts. An existence check inside a migration is an idempotent migration, recorded in the migration history like any other, not runtime schema creation.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Test support builds a throw-away in-memory PostgreSQL emulation and applies the real versioned migrations to it: the test path exercises the migrations rather than bypassing them.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The Job runs the compiled migration command (knex `migrate.latest` over the versioned migrations) before each rollout, and the deploy workflow waits for it: this is the versioned migration path.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The client package controls its surface: an `exports` map with `types` and `import` conditions for the root entry (and the manifest), a `files` allow-list of the build output and `sideEffects: false`. (The package's version number is LIB-001's matter, not this trap's: these lines are its surface.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The service's workspace package is `private` and is never published; its placeholder version is not a library version and needs no semantic versioning.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Outside the default cucumber profile's paths, but executed: the `webhooks` profile loads it and CI runs that profile as its own step.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: `code.startsWith("EX") && !code.startsWith("EXR")`: the second operand is negated, so it narrows the first (exceptions except the resolved-exception code) and is not implied by it.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The worker's HTTPS egress is `0.0.0.0/0` on port 443 only, with the private ranges and the link-local metadata range excepted. Merchant webhook endpoints are arbitrary public HTTPS URLs, so this is the narrowest rule that lets the worker do its job, not an open egress.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The API's ingress policy declares only `Ingress`. That is not missing egress control: the namespace default-deny policy denies egress for every pod and the API's allowances are separate policies.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Repository-level: no workload declares an explicit AppArmor or SELinux profile. That is not a confinement defect: on AppArmor-enabled nodes the container runtime applies its default profile unless a manifest opts out, the restricted Pod Security profile does not require an explicit one, and both Deployments set RuntimeDefault seccomp. (The migration Job's missing seccomp profile is a located plant, CNF-001.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Repository-level: the repository commits no Falco or Tetragon runtime threat detection. Runtime detection is a cluster-operator control deployed once per cluster, not something an application repository ships; its absence here is not a defect of this repository. (The namespace's missing admission enforcement is a located plant, ADM-001.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The carrier client bounds every attempt with AbortSignal.timeout (combined with the caller's signal) and retries transient failures with capped exponential backoff.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A published client library takes the caller's AbortSignal and an injectable fetch, and leaves timeout and retry policy to the host application; hard-wiring retries in a library is the wrong design.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: `/healthz` and `/readyz` are anonymous so the kubelet can probe them; they return no data.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: `/.well-known/security.txt` (RFC 9116) must be publicly readable.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A constant message split into two string literals joined with `+` for line length, with the values in the pino object argument: structured.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The image runs only on Kubernetes, which ignores a Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK; liveness and readiness probes are declared in the Deployments.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The API's and the worker's database allowance: one CIDR, one port. With DNS (allowed separately) it is the API's whole egress - the shape of a correct least-privilege egress policy, written with an ipBlock because the database is outside the cluster.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: `service.redirect(...)` redirects a PARCEL to a pickup point (a database update); no HTTP redirect is issued anywhere in the handler, so no user input reaches a Location header. (The unvalidated body two lines up is RDY-004, a different defect.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Secrets reach the container as environment variables through secretKeyRef. The application reads its configuration from the environment (validated at start-up, never logged); secrets as files are a hardening preference, not a misconfiguration.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: As TRP-023, for the worker's secretKeyRef environment variables.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: As TRP-023, for the migration Job's database URL.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The image is the team's own, from its organisation's GitHub container registry, pinned by digest and admitted only by digest (the namespace admission policy); there is no other registry the team could be asked to use.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: As TRP-026, for the worker.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: As TRP-026, for the migration Job.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The cucumber world imports the shared test database helper. Both are test code (specifications are a second test suite of the same service); no production module depends on test code.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: As TRP-029, for the webhook step definitions.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: cucumber's configuration file: cucumber-js loads it by name from the package directory (the `test:bdd` scripts); nothing imports a runner's configuration.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Step definitions are loaded by cucumber through the `import` globs of cucumber.mjs and run by both profiles; they are never imported by name.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: As TRP-032; run by the `webhooks` profile.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: cucumber's support code (world, hooks), loaded by the `import` globs of cucumber.mjs.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Repository-level: the claim that the service has no named authorization policies is untrue. The scopes are named once (`Scopes` in src/http/auth.ts) and every guarded route declares its scope at registration with `requireScope(Scopes.x)` - the TypeScript equivalent of a named policy. (The one unguarded route is a located plant, RDY-003.)

entries.rationale: Repository-level properties certified clean. Dependencies: every direct package is the current release of its line, maintained, non-deprecated, stable, permissively licensed, used where it is declared and declared where it is used (development tools only in devDependencies), and npm audit reports nothing; Node.js 22 is supported. No secret was ever committed. Every CI action is pinned by commit SHA and every image by digest; Dependabot has a cooldown. TypeScript strict mode everywhere; no module cycles; no floating promises; no skipped or assertion-free tests.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Default-deny ingress and egress for the namespace, DNS and per-flow allowances for the API and the worker; dented by the migration Job's unrestricted egress (EGR-001).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: RuntimeDefault seccomp on both Deployments, none on the migration Job (CNF-001); no explicit MAC profiles, which is not a defect (TRP-013).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: A namespaced admission policy requiring image digests is enforced, but Pod Security admission is warn/audit only (ADM-001); runtime detection is the cluster operator's (TRP-014).

entries.label: score-band
